definitions.explanation: An item that has been lost by its owner. A formal term used in official, legal, and transportation contexts such as train stations and police offices.

examples.japanese: {遺失物|いしつぶつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{届|とど}け{出|で}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I filed a lost property report.

examples.japanese: {遺失物|いしつぶつ}{取扱所|とりあつかいじょ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{二階|にかい}→二階：27513_nikai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: The lost and found office is on the second floor of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦{警察|けいさつ}→警察：01393_keisatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{届|とど}けられた→届ける：01248_todokeru⟧{遺失物|いしつぶつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧か{月|げつ}⟦{保管|ほかん}される→保管する：25536_hokansuru⟧。
examples.english: Lost property turned in to the police is kept for three months.

notes:
USAGE:
This is the formal, official term seen on signs at train stations, airports, and police stations. In everyday conversation, ⟦{落|お}とし{物|もの}→落とし物：08450_otoshimono⟧ or ⟦{忘|わす}れ{物|もの}→忘れ物：01758_wasuremono⟧ are more commonly used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遺失物|いしつぶつ}{取扱所|とりあつかいじょ} (lost and found office)
- {遺失物|いしつぶつ}{届|とどけ} (lost property report)
- {遺失物|いしつぶつ}⟦{法|ほう}→法：13620_hou⟧ (Lost Property Act)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{落|お}とし{物|もの}→落とし物：08450_otoshimono⟧: something dropped; casual equivalent
- ⟦{忘|わす}れ{物|もの}→忘れ物：01758_wasuremono⟧: something left behind; more common in daily speech
